 Advertisement Subtropical Storm Josephine brings coastal flooding to East Coast
 The nor'easter, now named Subtropical Storm Josephine, will bring dangerous conditions for multiple days this week.
 By Jonathan Erdman and Rob Shackelford • 8 hours ago Updated: October 22, 2026, 6:15 am EDT Published: October 22, 2026, 6:12 am EDT Share Share
 1 . Where will Subtropical Storm Josephine go? Chevron Down Subtropical Storm Josephine lashes East Coast with winds, waves
 An October nor'easter is still hugging the Atlantic coast, and the National Hurricane Center officially named the system Subtropical Storm Josephine .
 Even though the storm has been named Josephine, the impacts will be the same as if it were only a nor'easter.
 (MORE: What is a subtropical storm? | Josephine tracker )

 Josephine is expected to stay well offshore as it moves northeastward. It will strengthen slightly, potentially reaching sustained winds of 80 mph on Friday. The heaviest winds and rain will stay offshore, but rip currents could be life-threatening the rest of the week.
 (MORE: 'This job can kill you': Meet the people on the wildfire frontlines ) 
 Impacts from Josephine
 While we do not expect Josephine to be as impactful as the late September nor'easter , we need to remain cautious across the East Coast. Let's break down the main takeaways:

 Coastal flooding 
 The area most likely to see prolonged coastal flooding is from the Delmarva Peninsula to eastern North Carolina.
 Coastal flood alerts are in effect for North Carolina's Outer Banks, where anywhere from 1 to 4 feet of inundation is possible. High surf advisories are also in place across the North Carolina coastline, with waves potentially reaching up to 14 feet.
 Across parts of the Virginia, Maryland, Delaware and New Jersey coasts, inundation up to 2 feet and large waves as high as 10 feet are possible.
 Water levels across river gauges from North Carolina to Maryland could rise to moderate flood stage at high tide.
 High surf, coastal flooding and rip currents are expected to stretch as far south as Florida's Atlantic beaches and as far north as New England's coastline. Expect significant beach erosion across the East Coast this week.
 Winds and rain 
 The worst gusts have shifted from the Carolinas to New England as Josephine shifts north. Gusts could still knock down power lines across coastal communities.
 This storm shouldn't be a huge rainmaker; most of the heavy rain is forecast to stay offshore. However, there could be some off-and-on showers, mainly for coastal areas.
